note: Reflexion playbook for the rule extractor. Add a lesson as 'pending'; only a person may set 'approved' (with reviewed_by) or 'rejected' (with rejection_reason). Only approved lessons reach the prompt. Learn lessons from development schemes only, then set frozen to true before the held-out run.

lessons.lesson: write a separate yes/no rule for the kind of person as well as the two age rules; do not treat the person type as implied by the age range.
lessons.applies_when: one sentence names a kind of person and an age range together (for example a widow aged 40 to 79)

lessons.lesson: make each rule's source_quote a short phrase copied exactly from the passage for that one category; never join, shorten or reword items, because a quote that is not word for word is discarded with its rule.
lessons.applies_when: a passage lists several categories in one long paragraph

lessons.lesson: use a field only if the clause itself states that condition; do not add a rule because a similar-sounding field exists (a farmer's family is not the family of a deceased person), and do not add residence or state rules the text does not state.
lessons.applies_when: you are choosing a field for a clause

lessons.lesson: write a rule for owning on that date or for being listed in those records; set needs_human_review to true if the passage also gives exceptions.
lessons.applies_when: a passage fixes a cut-off date for ownership or says a name must appear in official records
lessons.rejection_reason: the lesson is too specific to a single scheme; it is not a generalizable rule for the extractor.
